The question

Can you tell a wrong logic translation from a right one without a gold formula?

A sentence has many correct translations, gold formulas are rare, and a fair share of the published ones are wrong. The paper asks whether agreement among independent translators can stand in for the gold. Several LLM translate the same sentence; checks which of their formulas are logically equivalent to the candidate after ; the is the share of peers that disagree.

The answer: on 2,686 real translations from nine model families, consensus reaches , against for the pre-registered . Added to a , it still raises AUROC by , so it carries signal the baselines lack.

        Does a meaning-preserving rewrite trigger a false alarm?

        Share of z3-equivalent rewrites of correct base formulas that each metric flags (PERTURB controls, thresholds fixed on development set E). A renamed predicate means the same thing, so an ideal metric would stay at its base rate. is the paper's attempt to fix this.

        Metrics shown

        What the paper does not show

        • No fresh confirmation. The pre-registered test on a new held-out set (E2) was stopped by budget. Only 110 of 550 sentences received panel labels, and the long-sentence stratum shrank to 94 rows (76 ERROR, 18 CORRECT). On the 273 testable rows, mostly ProverQA sentences, consensus reaches AUROC 0.890 and ties a local 8B judge (0.913; delta +0.003 [−0.042, 0.052]).
        • No advantage on short sentences. On the FOLIO CTRL stratum the difference is −0.069 [−0.23, 0.10]. The confirmed advantage is specific to sentences with at least 20 words and at least 3 conditions.
        • Rename invariance is unsolved. Name-free matching cuts nonce-rename false alarms to 0.132 but lowers AUROC to 0.686. A gloss-gated hybrid failed its development gate (checker balanced accuracy 0.780 against a 0.90 threshold).
        • Labels shape the ranking. Primary labels are z3 equivalence to audited gold, which can count vocabulary mismatches as errors. Under panel-adjudicated intent labels, the frontier judge's lead over the cheap judge grows by +0.166 [0.086, 0.244].
        • Candidate-signature peers do not help. Giving peers the candidate's own symbols lowers d (0.139 vs 0.323) but raises e (0.459 vs 0.173), and stratified AUROC falls to 0.614. Consensus needs independent translations.
